(Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- crypto-privacy-reviewer: Cryptography and privacy expert that reviews code, validates assumptions, and generates test cases. NOT prefixed with gsd- so it survives GSD updates. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write)

## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via "pencil" MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Always call get_editor_state(include_schema: true) if you don't have the current .pen file schema in the context. Knowing the schema is required to use any other Pencil MCP tool.

Tools: get_editor_state, get_guidelines, batch_get, batch_design, snapshot_layout, get_screenshot, get_variables, export_nodes, export_html.

{"body":"## Goal
Close the facade read-surface gap that blocks the whole web browser. Today `Engine` is command-in / event-out only and `SnapshotUpdated` is a payload-free ping — the v1 UI harvest can render nothing until a key-free read surface lands. This is the natural successor to #789.

## Harvest / create
- `Engine::snapshot(folder) -> SnapshotView` projected from `sync/model::Snapshot`, **key-free**: root id; focused folder direct-children `{id,name,kind,size?,mtime?,pending,deadLetter,contentVersion}`; ancestor chain to root for breadcrumbs; current `Staleness`.
- `Engine::read_content(node) -> Bytes`.
- Per-node `pending`/`deadLetter` + an `OpProgress{opId,node,phase,error?}` channel for upload/download rows.

## Rewire
- `crates/wasm/src/host.rs` — expose `snapshot` / `download`.
- `packages/client` — `worker/protocol.ts`, `worker/commandCodec.ts`, `transport.ts`, `broadcastTransport.ts`, `facade.ts` read paths.

## Engine seams
`snapshot`, `read_content`/`download`, `OpProgress` channel.

## Tests
Rust projection unit tests + `packages/client` browser conformance over both transports (direct + broadcast).

## Gate
`cargo test` + `packages/client` browser suite.

## Depends on
None.

I now have everything needed. Here is the structured report.

---

# Codebase Map for Issue #802 — Snapshot/Read Surface

Base commit: PR #789 merged as `5856c5bd9`. Current `main` HEAD `7f17bd24c`. Nothing named `SnapshotView`, `OpProgress`, `read_content`, or `download` exists yet — #802 introduces all of them. What exists today is the scaffolding they attach to.

## 1. crates/engine — the Engine facade (from #789)

### Public API — commands in / events out
Everything lives in `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`, re-exported through `crates/engine/src/lib.rs:57-60`.

**Engine handle** (`facade.rs:593-636`): `Engine<T: SeamTypes>`. Constructed via `Engine::new(seams, entropy, profile, api_base_url, gateway) -> (Self, EventStream)` (`facade.rs:641-668`). Key internal state:
- `snapshot: Rc<RefCell<Snapshot>>` (`facade.rs:615`) — the last-known-good gate-passing base snapshot, seeded to `Snapshot::new(NodeId([0u8;16]))`, repainted in place by the resolve-tick loop.
- `held_records`, `alive`, `session: Option<Rc<SessionIdentity>>`, `api`, `gateway: Gateway`, `events: mpsc::UnboundedSender<Event>`.

**Public methods:**
- `async start(&mut self, secret: LoginSecret) -> Result<(), EngineError>` (`facade.rs:684`) — cold-start pipeline: derives session, logs in, runs `cold_start_data_path`, sets base snapshot, spawns liveness + resolve-tick loops.
- `async command(&mut self, command: Command) -> Result<(), EngineError>` (`facade.rs:1030`) — the single write entry point. Only `Create` (metadata-only), `Delete`, `Rename`, `Relink`, `SiweLogin` are implemented; all others return `EngineError::Unimplemented`. Content-bearing creates and `UpdateContent` are explicitly `Unimplemented` (`facade.rs:1045-1049`).
- `async view(&self) -> Result<EngineView, EngineError>` (`facade.rs:1092`) — **the existing read surface**. Returns `EngineView` (`facade.rs:482-524`) wrapping the rendered `Snapshot`; offers FUSE-shaped `root()`, `children(parent) -> Vec<NodeAttrs>`, `lookup(parent, name)`, `attrs(node)`, `statfs()`. This is the key-bearing internal projection that #802's key-free `SnapshotView` will parallel/replace at the WASM boundary.
- `fn root(&self) -> NodeId` (`facade.rs:1103`), `fn profile(&self)` (`facade.rs:1170`).

**Command enum** (`facade.rs:178-293`): `Create{parent,name,kind,content:Option<PlaintextContent>}`, `Delete`, `Rename`, `Relink`, `UpdateContent`, `SetFocus{node:Option<NodeId>}`, `ManualRefresh`, `ImportContact`, `Grant`, `Revoke`, `Downgrade`, `CreateInviteLink`, `AcceptShare`, `RotateNow`, `SiweLogin`, `Logout`. Hand-written `Debug` prints variant name only (`facade.rs:319-323`).

**Event enum** (`facade.rs:328-364`): `SnapshotUpdated` (payload-free), `StalenessChanged{level:Staleness}`, `WithheldUpdateEscalation{ipns_name:Vec<u8>}`, `DeadLetter{op_id:OpId}`, `AttributableAbuse{description:String}`, `RenewalFailed{routing_key,detail}`. **These are all payload-minimal today** — `SnapshotUpdated` carries no data; the host must call `view()` to read state. #802's per-node pending/deadLetter overlay and `OpProgress` channel are not represented in this enum yet.

`EventStream` (`facade.rs:466-475`): `async next() -> Option<Event>` over an unbounded mpsc receiver.

`NodeAttrs` (`facade.rs:90-100`): `{id, name, kind, content_version:u64}` — note it has **no size/mtime** ("content size and timestamps land with the content-plane slice", `facade.rs:88-89`). #802's `{id,name,kind,size?,mtime?,pending,deadLetter,contentVersion}` extends this.

### How SnapshotUpdated is emitted today
Four sites, all fire-and-forget over the events channel:
1. Cold-start boot, after first projection — `crates/engine/src/sync/boot.rs:164,216`.
2. Resolve-tick loop, when a gate-passing `Adopted` repaints the base cell — `facade.rs:1011-1012` (guarded by `refresh_base_from_outcome`).
3. Metadata op staged — `stage_and_notify` at `facade.rs:1160`.
4. It is a bare push-invalidation trigger: hosts re-`view()` on receipt. There is no per-node pending/deadLetter flag on the wire.

### sync/model::Snapshot — exact structure
`crates/engine/src/sync/model.rs`:
- `Snapshot` (`model.rs:65-71`): `{ root: NodeId, nodes: BTreeMap<NodeId,NodeMeta> (private), links: Vec<Link> (private) }`.
- `NodeMeta` (`model.rs:21-36`): `{ id: NodeId, name: String (as-entered), kind: NodeKind, record_sequence: u64, content_version: u64 }`. **No size, no mtime fields exist.** `content_version` is here.
- `Link` (`model.rs:52-61`): `{ parent, child, link_counter: u64 }` (dual-link tiebreak).
- Accessor methods #802 will lean on: `node(id)`, `children(parent) -> Vec<&NodeMeta>` (sorted by id, `model.rs:201-213`), `ancestors(node) -> Vec<NodeId>` (nearest-first to root, cycle-guarded, `model.rs:218-231`), `parent_of`, `record_sequence`, `contains`.
- `collation_key(name)` (`model.rs:268`) — the strict name comparator.

**Projection into Snapshot**: `crates/engine/src/sync/project.rs` — `project_root(root, adopted) -> Snapshot` (`project.rs:20-35`) lifts direct children only from `ReadBody::Folder{children,...}`, carrying `child.name`, `map_kind(child.kind)`, `child.link_counter`. Root sequence set from `adopted.sequence`. Size/mtime not projected (the `ReadBody::Folder` also carries `created_at`/`modified_at` but they are discarded — see `project.rs:66-76` test).

**Rendering (base ⊕ overlay)**: `Engine::render()` (`facade.rs:1108-1114`) = `apply_overlay(&base, &pending_ops)`. `pending_ops()` (`facade.rs:1119-1128`) reads the durable staging store, `decode_queue`s it FIFO, drops undecodables.

### Pending ops / dead-letter tracking (offline op queue)
- The durable op queue is the **StagingStore seam** (`crates/engine/src/seams/staging_store.rs`); `OpId(pub u64)` defined at `staging_store.rs:8`.
- Ops staged via `stage_op` (`crates/engine/src/sync/staging.rs`), returning `StageOutcome::Queued{..}` / `RejectedOverBudget{..}` (`facade.rs:1153-1166`).
- Pending state is **not** tracked per-node today — it is a flat FIFO queue read on every render. There is no per-node "pending" or "deadLetter" boolean anywhere; #802 must derive these by diffing the overlay ops against the base per node.
- **Dead-letter** is surfaced only at cold-start: undecodable queue entries emit `Event::DeadLetter{op_id}` and are removed from the durable queue (gated on successful send) — `facade.rs:840-864`. Ops that terminally fail rebase are documented to dead-letter (`facade.rs:344-348`) but the rebase-failure emission path is a later slice. `Op`/`OpKind` live in `crates/engine/src/sync/op.rs` (`OpKind` enum at `op.rs:35`).

### Content download/read path (existing fetch/decrypt)
The whole verified-fetch machinery `read_content` will compose already exists in `crates/engine/src/content/`:
- **`read_block(gateway, http, cid_str, expected_cid, plane) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ReadError>`** — `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:175-231`. Fetches one block over the ordered `Gateway` source set (token-authed accelerator first, then public fallbacks), CID-verifies via `cipherbox_core::content::verify_cid`, fail-closed `ReadError::TrustViolation` on mismatch, rotates on availability failure/over-cap, caps body size. `ReadError` = `TrustViolation | TooLarge | Unavailable` (`read.rs:128-150`).
- `Gateway`/`GatewaySource`/`GatewayConfig` (`read.rs:55-125`) — the engine holds a resolved `gateway: Gateway` field.
- `ContentPlane::{Leaf,Root}` (`read.rs:37-53`) pins the codec.
- `leaf_range_for_byte_range(offset,length,chunk_size,leaf_count)` (`read.rs:282-305`) — chunk-aligned range mapping.
- **DAG/manifest**: `RootManifest{chunk_size:u64, size:u64, leaf_cids:Vec<Vec<u8>>}` (`crates/engine/src/content/dag.rs:143-150`), `decode_root(root_block)` (`dag.rs:159`), `assemble` (`dag.rs:106`). `SealedContent{content_cid, root_block, leaves}` (`content/mod.rs:44-55`).

The ladder classifier is `classify(now, last_success, reconcile_in_flight, connectivity, profile) -> Staleness` in `crates/engine/src/sync/staleness.rs:41-65` (plus `withheld_escalation`, `staleness.rs:71-82`). `Connectivity{Online,Offline}` at `staleness.rs:22`. The WASM mirror enum is `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs:131-151`; the TS mirror is `packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts:26` (`'fresh'|'reconciling'|'stale'|'offline'`).

## 3. crates/wasm/src/host.rs — exposed surface & boundary patterns

`EngineHandle` (`host.rs:75-79`): `{ engine: Rc<Mutex<Engine<WebSeamTypes>>>, events: Rc<Mutex<EventStream>> }`. Exposed methods:
- `#[wasm_bindgen(constructor)] new(seams, profile, api_base_url, accelerator_base_url, accelerator_bearer, public_gateways)` (`host.rs:92-173`) — builds `SeamSet` by pulling each named seam off the JS bag (`take_seam`, `host.rs:65-72`); constructs `GatewayConfig` (bearer zeroized), `Engine::new`.
- `start(secret: Vec<u8>) -> Promise` (`host.rs:180-191`).
- `command(command: Command) -> Promise` (`host.rs:195-207`) — takes the boundary `Command`, `.into_facade()`, runs it under the async mutex.
- `#[wasm_bindgen(js_name = nextEvent)] next_event() -> Promise` (`host.rs:211-221`) — reads one event, wraps via `Event::from_facade(...).into()`, resolves `undefined` when the stream ends.

**Boundary value types & patterns** in `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs`:
- `NodeId` (`lib.rs:56-85`): opaque handle; `fromBytes(&[u8]) -> Result<NodeId,JsError>` (16-byte check) and `bytes() -> Vec<u8>` getter. This is the pattern #802's snapshot node ids follow.
- `Command` (`lib.rs:163-321`): opaque, built by static builders (`create`/`delete`/... mirroring facade), `into_facade()` for the host. No payload readback (intent-only).
- `Event` (`lib.rs:330-408`): read via `kind() -> String` discriminant (`"snapshotUpdated"`, `"stalenessChanged"`, etc., `lib.rs:339-349`) plus per-variant getters that return `Option<...>`/`undefined` off-variant: `staleness()`, `ipnsName()`, `opId() -> Option<u64>` (crosses as bigint), `description()`, `routingKey()`, `detail()`.
- **How bytes cross** (documented `lib.rs:11-17`): `u64` → `bigint`, binary payloads → `Uint8Array`, no secret key material crosses. `NodeId.bytes()` returns `Vec<u8>` (→ `Uint8Array`). #802's `read_content -> Bytes` will return a `Vec<u8>`/`Uint8Array`; the `SnapshotView` projection will be a new `#[wasm_bindgen]` value type with getters, since **no snapshot/view structure crosses the boundary today** (`lib.rs:14-17` — the entire view surface is deliberately absent).
- Exhaustive-match tests guard facade↔binding mapping at `lib.rs:428-499`; wasm-target boundary tests in `crates/wasm/tests/boundary.rs`.

## 4. packages/client — message/command shapes, event flow, read-path stubs, tests

**Wire protocol** `packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts`:
- `CommandDescriptor` (`protocol.ts:32-59`) — plain-data union, one variant per facade command; `kind` matches the wasm builder name. `u64`→`bigint`, binary→`Uint8Array`, file content→`ArrayBuffer` (transferred).
- `EventDescriptor` (`protocol.ts:62-67`) — `{kind:'snapshotUpdated'} | {kind:'stalenessChanged',staleness} | {kind:'withheldUpdateEscalation',ipnsName} | {kind:'deadLetter',opId:bigint} | {kind:'attributableAbuse',description}`. **Note `renewalFailed` is not mirrored here.** No view/snapshot descriptor exists — this is deliberate ("carries only intent... never snapshot/view state", `protocol.ts:8-12`).
- `WorkerRequest` (`protocol.ts:70-72`): only `start` and `command`. #802 must add snapshot/read request types here.
- `WorkerMessage` (`protocol.ts:75-84`): `ready | response{id,ok,...} | event{event} | fatal`.

**commandCodec** `packages/client/src/worker/commandCodec.ts`:
- `buildCommand(wasm, descriptor) -> WasmCommand` (`commandCodec.ts:31-91`) — exhaustive switch to wasm builders.
- `readEvent(wasm, event) -> EventDescriptor` (`commandCodec.ts:110-130`) — reads wasm `Event` getters into descriptors; fail-closed `throw` on unknown kind/staleness (`commandCodec.ts:104-106,125-128`). This is where #802 adds new event handling and where a snapshot/read decode would slot.

**Event flow**: worker → `EngineHost.nextEvent()` (`worker/engineHost.ts:48-51`, calls `readEvent`) → `serve.ts:50` pumps → posts `{type:'event',event}` → transport `emit()`. On the UI side, `LocalTransport` (`transport.ts:48-109`) correlates responses by monotonic id and calls `this.emit(message.event)` on `'event'` (`transport.ts:68`). `EngineFacade.subscribe(listener)` (`facade.ts:48-50`) exposes the stream.

**Read-path stubs**: **None exist.** `EngineFacade` (`facade.ts:16-127`) has one method per write command plus `start`/`logout`/`subscribe`/`manualRefresh` — no `snapshot()` / `read()` / `download()` method. `EngineTransport` interface (`transport.ts:23-32`) has only `start`/`command`/`subscribe`/`close`. `WasmEngineHandle` (`worker/engineWasm.ts:29-33`) exposes only `start`/`command`/`nextEvent`. #802 adds new methods across all four (`engineWasm.ts` handle type, `engineHost.ts`, `transport.ts`, `facade.ts`).

**Test setup**:
- **Node/vitest unit tests** (`pnpm test` → `vitest run`): `facade.test.ts` (FakeTransport, `facade.test.ts:7-33`), `transport.test.ts` (FakeWorker replaying WorkerMessages, `transport.test.ts:6-36`), `broadcastTransport.test.ts`, `leadership.test.ts`, `engineClient.test.ts`, `index.test.ts`.

  - `conformance.spec.ts` — per-**seam** engine conformance kits over real IndexedDB/OPFS (floorStore, snapshotCache, stagingStore, credentialStore, scheduler, recordTransport) via a `window.runSeam` harness.
  - `engine.spec.ts` — the engine-worker RPC slice: cold-start/logout, out-of-order correlation, event-stream ordering, the `u64`/bigint + transfer boundary, WASM-backed detachment cases (via `window.runRealEngine`/`runBoundary`).
  - `leadership.spec.ts` — leader/follower.
  - The wasm build is driven by `test/browser/build-wasm.mjs` with `--features conformance` (`crates/wasm/src/conformance.rs`, gated at `lib.rs:47-48`). #802's snapshot/read boundary and the "direct + broadcast transport" conformance the issue references would extend `engine.spec.ts`/`leadership.spec.ts` here.

**blueprint/engine.md:**
- Sync core state law — `engine.md:189-191`: *"rendered state = last-known-good remote snapshot ⊕ pending-op overlay, single owner; the op queue is the only local divergence (#33 D6)."*
- Focus-window tick — `engine.md:192-197`: *"refresh the vault pointer, the open folder, and its full ancestor chain to root"* — the exact focus/ancestor surface #802 projects.
- Ops list — `engine.md:208-209`: *"every mutation is an intent op — create, delete, rename, relink, updateContent — carrying its base sequence, journaled FIFO in the durable op queue."*
- Content plane reads — `engine.md:479-482`: *"the token-authed trustless gateway is a member accelerator; any public trustless gateway is the no-auth fallback. The engine verifies CIDs client-side via core on every block/CAR response; media uses ranged fetches."* (This is exactly what `read_content`/`download` will drive.)
- Facade — `engine.md:494-502`: *"one async command-and-event surface, designed to be wrapped, not extended: commands ... and an event stream out (snapshot updates, staleness transitions, withheld-update escalations, dead-letters, attributable abuse events). ... hosts render, they never decide."* No `SnapshotView`/`OpProgress` is named in the blueprint by that term — #802 introduces the vocabulary.

**blueprint/web-client.md:**

- Progressive hydration — `web-client.md:145-147`: *"name and kind render instantly from the parent's child refs (#27 D7); **size/mtime arrive as child resolves land in the snapshot** — no blocking resolution pass, no kind-flip UX."* — the normative basis for `size?`/`mtime?` being optional in `SnapshotView`.

- Upload/op progress — `web-client.md:193-194`: *"Per-file progress/error is **event-stream state on the upload's op id**; cancel is a facade command killing the op before publish."* — the normative basis for #802's `OpProgress{opId,node,phase,error?}`.
- Wire hygiene — `web-client.md:96-98`: *"projections and events are plain structured-clone data; commands carry at most Blob/File handles."* And `web-client.md:114-117`: *"wasm-bindgen types end to end. Commands are the engine facade's commands verbatim; the client adds transport, never semantics."*
- Testing hooks — `web-client.md:229-239`: `packages/client` (leadership, failover, both transports, seams) is a **CI-blocking browser test surface**; a DEV-gated facade introspection hook (snapshot + event-stream taps, no key access) is the e2e seam.

- `OpProgress`: **none** (new in #802). Closest existing concept: `StageOutcome` (`sync/staging.rs`), `Event::DeadLetter`, `Event::RenewalFailed`.

# Codebase Map for Issue #802 — Snapshot/Read Surface

Base commit: PR #789 merged as `5856c5bd9`. Current `main` HEAD `7f17bd24c`. Nothing named `SnapshotView`, `OpProgress`, `read_content`, or `download` exists yet — #802 introduces all of them. What exists today is the scaffolding they attach to.

## 1. crates/engine — the Engine facade (from #789)

### Public API — commands in / events out
Everything lives in `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`, re-exported through `crates/engine/src/lib.rs:57-60`.

**Engine handle** (`facade.rs:593-636`): `Engine<T: SeamTypes>`. Constructed via `Engine::new(seams, entropy, profile, api_base_url, gateway) -> (Self, EventStream)` (`facade.rs:641-668`). Key internal state:
- `snapshot: Rc<RefCell<Snapshot>>` (`facade.rs:615`) — the last-known-good gate-passing base snapshot, seeded to `Snapshot::new(NodeId([0u8;16]))`, repainted in place by the resolve-tick loop.
- `held_records`, `alive`, `session: Option<Rc<SessionIdentity>>`, `api`, `gateway: Gateway`, `events: mpsc::UnboundedSender<Event>`.

**Public methods:**
- `async start(&mut self, secret: LoginSecret) -> Result<(), EngineError>` (`facade.rs:684`) — cold-start pipeline: derives session, logs in, runs `cold_start_data_path`, sets base snapshot, spawns liveness + resolve-tick loops.
- `async command(&mut self, command: Command) -> Result<(), EngineError>` (`facade.rs:1030`) — the single write entry point. Only `Create` (metadata-only), `Delete`, `Rename`, `Relink`, `SiweLogin` are implemented; all others return `EngineError::Unimplemented`. Content-bearing creates and `UpdateContent` are explicitly `Unimplemented` (`facade.rs:1045-1049`).
- `async view(&self) -> Result<EngineView, EngineError>` (`facade.rs:1092`) — **the existing read surface**. Returns `EngineView` (`facade.rs:482-524`) wrapping the rendered `Snapshot`; offers FUSE-shaped `root()`, `children(parent) -> Vec<NodeAttrs>`, `lookup(parent, name)`, `attrs(node)`, `statfs()`. This is the key-bearing internal projection that #802's key-free `SnapshotView` will parallel/replace at the WASM boundary.
- `fn root(&self) -> NodeId` (`facade.rs:1103`), `fn profile(&self)` (`facade.rs:1170`).

**Command enum** (`facade.rs:178-293`): `Create{parent,name,kind,content:Option<PlaintextContent>}`, `Delete`, `Rename`, `Relink`, `UpdateContent`, `SetFocus{node:Option<NodeId>}`, `ManualRefresh`, `ImportContact`, `Grant`, `Revoke`, `Downgrade`, `CreateInviteLink`, `AcceptShare`, `RotateNow`, `SiweLogin`, `Logout`. Hand-written `Debug` prints variant name only (`facade.rs:319-323`).

**Event enum** (`facade.rs:328-364`): `SnapshotUpdated` (payload-free), `StalenessChanged{level:Staleness}`, `WithheldUpdateEscalation{ipns_name:Vec<u8>}`, `DeadLetter{op_id:OpId}`, `AttributableAbuse{description:String}`, `RenewalFailed{routing_key,detail}`. **These are all payload-minimal today** — `SnapshotUpdated` carries no data; the host must call `view()` to read state. #802's per-node pending/deadLetter overlay and `OpProgress` channel are not represented in this enum yet.

`EventStream` (`facade.rs:466-475`): `async next() -> Option<Event>` over an unbounded mpsc receiver.

`NodeAttrs` (`facade.rs:90-100`): `{id, name, kind, content_version:u64}` — note it has **no size/mtime** ("content size and timestamps land with the content-plane slice", `facade.rs:88-89`). #802's `{id,name,kind,size?,mtime?,pending,deadLetter,contentVersion}` extends this.

### How SnapshotUpdated is emitted today
Four sites, all fire-and-forget over the events channel:
1. Cold-start boot, after first projection — `crates/engine/src/sync/boot.rs:164,216`.
2. Resolve-tick loop, when a gate-passing `Adopted` repaints the base cell — `facade.rs:1011-1012` (guarded by `refresh_base_from_outcome`).
3. Metadata op staged — `stage_and_notify` at `facade.rs:1160`.
4. It is a bare push-invalidation trigger: hosts re-`view()` on receipt. There is no per-node pending/deadLetter flag on the wire.

### sync/model::Snapshot — exact structure
`crates/engine/src/sync/model.rs`:
- `Snapshot` (`model.rs:65-71`): `{ root: NodeId, nodes: BTreeMap<NodeId,NodeMeta> (private), links: Vec<Link> (private) }`.
- `NodeMeta` (`model.rs:21-36`): `{ id: NodeId, name: String (as-entered), kind: NodeKind, record_sequence: u64, content_version: u64 }`. **No size, no mtime fields exist.** `content_version` is here.
- `Link` (`model.rs:52-61`): `{ parent, child, link_counter: u64 }` (dual-link tiebreak).
- Accessor methods #802 will lean on: `node(id)`, `children(parent) -> Vec<&NodeMeta>` (sorted by id, `model.rs:201-213`), `ancestors(node) -> Vec<NodeId>` (nearest-first to root, cycle-guarded, `model.rs:218-231`), `parent_of`, `record_sequence`, `contains`.
- `collation_key(name)` (`model.rs:268`) — the strict name comparator.

**Projection into Snapshot**: `crates/engine/src/sync/project.rs` — `project_root(root, adopted) -> Snapshot` (`project.rs:20-35`) lifts direct children only from `ReadBody::Folder{children,...}`, carrying `child.name`, `map_kind(child.kind)`, `child.link_counter`. Root sequence set from `adopted.sequence`. Size/mtime not projected (the `ReadBody::Folder` also carries `created_at`/`modified_at` but they are discarded — see `project.rs:66-76` test).

**Rendering (base ⊕ overlay)**: `Engine::render()` (`facade.rs:1108-1114`) = `apply_overlay(&base, &pending_ops)`. `pending_ops()` (`facade.rs:1119-1128`) reads the durable staging store, `decode_queue`s it FIFO, drops undecodables.

### Pending ops / dead-letter tracking (offline op queue)
- The durable op queue is the **StagingStore seam** (`crates/engine/src/seams/staging_store.rs`); `OpId(pub u64)` defined at `staging_store.rs:8`.
- Ops staged via `stage_op` (`crates/engine/src/sync/staging.rs`), returning `StageOutcome::Queued{..}` / `RejectedOverBudget{..}` (`facade.rs:1153-1166`).
- Pending state is **not** tracked per-node today — it is a flat FIFO queue read on every render. There is no per-node "pending" or "deadLetter" boolean anywhere; #802 must derive these by diffing the overlay ops against the base per node.
- **Dead-letter** is surfaced only at cold-start: undecodable queue entries emit `Event::DeadLetter{op_id}` and are removed from the durable queue (gated on successful send) — `facade.rs:840-864`. Ops that terminally fail rebase are documented to dead-letter (`facade.rs:344-348`) but the rebase-failure emission path is a later slice. `Op`/`OpKind` live in `crates/engine/src/sync/op.rs` (`OpKind` enum at `op.rs:35`).

The whole verified-fetch machinery `read_content` will compose already exists in `crates/engine/src/content/`:
- **`read_block(gateway, http, cid_str, expected_cid, plane) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ReadError>`** — `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:175-231`. Fetches one block over the ordered `Gateway` source set (token-authed accelerator first, then public fallbacks), CID-verifies via `cipherbox_core::content::verify_cid`, fail-closed `ReadError::TrustViolation` on mismatch, rotates on availability failure/over-cap, caps body size. `ReadError` = `TrustViolation | TooLarge | Unavailable` (`read.rs:128-150`).
- `Gateway`/`GatewaySource`/`GatewayConfig` (`read.rs:55-125`) — the engine holds a resolved `gateway: Gateway` field.
- `ContentPlane::{Leaf,Root}` (`read.rs:37-53`) pins the codec.
- `leaf_range_for_byte_range(offset,length,chunk_size,leaf_count)` (`read.rs:282-305`) — chunk-aligned range mapping.
- **DAG/manifest**: `RootManifest{chunk_size:u64, size:u64, leaf_cids:Vec<Vec<u8>>}` (`crates/engine/src/content/dag.rs:143-150`), `decode_root(root_block)` (`dag.rs:159`), `assemble` (`dag.rs:106`). `SealedContent{content_cid, root_block, leaves}` (`content/mod.rs:44-55`).
- **Missing link for #802**: there is no per-node mapping from a `NodeId` to its `contentCid`/version root today — `NodeMeta` carries only `content_version:u64`, not a content CID. `read_content(node)` will need to source the version's `contentCid` (the read-body content plane assembly "lands with a later slice" per `sync/model.rs:5-6` and `project.rs:3-4`). Chunk-open/decrypt primitives (`open_chunk`, `ContentKey`) exist in `content/chunk.rs`.

## 2. Staleness — type & definition
`enum Staleness { Fresh, Reconciling, Stale, Offline }` — defined in `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:123-133`, re-exported at `lib.rs:59`. The ladder classifier is `classify(now, last_success, reconcile_in_flight, connectivity, profile) -> Staleness` in `crates/engine/src/sync/staleness.rs:41-65` (plus `withheld_escalation`, `staleness.rs:71-82`). `Connectivity{Online,Offline}` at `staleness.rs:22`. The WASM mirror enum is `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs:131-151`; the TS mirror is `packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts:26` (`'fresh'|'reconciling'|'stale'|'offline'`).

## 3. crates/wasm/src/host.rs — exposed surface & boundary patterns

`EngineHandle` (`host.rs:75-79`): `{ engine: Rc<Mutex<Engine<WebSeamTypes>>>, events: Rc<Mutex<EventStream>> }`. Exposed methods:
- `#[wasm_bindgen(constructor)] new(seams, profile, api_base_url, accelerator_base_url, accelerator_bearer, public_gateways)` (`host.rs:92-173`) — builds `SeamSet` by pulling each named seam off the JS bag (`take_seam`, `host.rs:65-72`); constructs `GatewayConfig` (bearer zeroized), `Engine::new`.
- `start(secret: Vec<u8>) -> Promise` (`host.rs:180-191`).
- `command(command: Command) -> Promise` (`host.rs:195-207`) — takes the boundary `Command`, `.into_facade()`, runs it under the async mutex.
- `#[wasm_bindgen(js_name = nextEvent)] next_event() -> Promise` (`host.rs:211-221`) — reads one event, wraps via `Event::from_facade(...).into()`, resolves `undefined` when the stream ends.

**Boundary value types & patterns** in `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs`:
- `NodeId` (`lib.rs:56-85`): opaque handle; `fromBytes(&[u8]) -> Result<NodeId,JsError>` (16-byte check) and `bytes() -> Vec<u8>` getter. This is the pattern #802's snapshot node ids follow.
- `Command` (`lib.rs:163-321`): opaque, built by static builders (`create`/`delete`/... mirroring facade), `into_facade()` for the host. No payload readback (intent-only).
- `Event` (`lib.rs:330-408`): read via `kind() -> String` discriminant (`"snapshotUpdated"`, `"stalenessChanged"`, etc., `lib.rs:339-349`) plus per-variant getters that return `Option<...>`/`undefined` off-variant: `staleness()`, `ipnsName()`, `opId() -> Option<u64>` (crosses as bigint), `description()`, `routingKey()`, `detail()`.
- **How bytes cross** (documented `lib.rs:11-17`): `u64` → `bigint`, binary payloads → `Uint8Array`, no secret key material crosses. `NodeId.bytes()` returns `Vec<u8>` (→ `Uint8Array`). #802's `read_content -> Bytes` will return a `Vec<u8>`/`Uint8Array`; the `SnapshotView` projection will be a new `#[wasm_bindgen]` value type with getters, since **no snapshot/view structure crosses the boundary today** (`lib.rs:14-17` — the entire view surface is deliberately absent).
- Exhaustive-match tests guard facade↔binding mapping at `lib.rs:428-499`; wasm-target boundary tests in `crates/wasm/tests/boundary.rs`.

## 4. packages/client — message/command shapes, event flow, read-path stubs, tests

**Wire protocol** `packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts`:
- `CommandDescriptor` (`protocol.ts:32-59`) — plain-data union, one variant per facade command; `kind` matches the wasm builder name. `u64`→`bigint`, binary→`Uint8Array`, file content→`ArrayBuffer` (transferred).
- `EventDescriptor` (`protocol.ts:62-67`) — `{kind:'snapshotUpdated'} | {kind:'stalenessChanged',staleness} | {kind:'withheldUpdateEscalation',ipnsName} | {kind:'deadLetter',opId:bigint} | {kind:'attributableAbuse',description}`. **Note `renewalFailed` is not mirrored here.** No view/snapshot descriptor exists — this is deliberate ("carries only intent... never snapshot/view state", `protocol.ts:8-12`).
- `WorkerRequest` (`protocol.ts:70-72`): only `start` and `command`. #802 must add snapshot/read request types here.
- `WorkerMessage` (`protocol.ts:75-84`): `ready | response{id,ok,...} | event{event} | fatal`.

**commandCodec** `packages/client/src/worker/commandCodec.ts`:
- `buildCommand(wasm, descriptor) -> WasmCommand` (`commandCodec.ts:31-91`) — exhaustive switch to wasm builders.
- `readEvent(wasm, event) -> EventDescriptor` (`commandCodec.ts:110-130`) — reads wasm `Event` getters into descriptors; fail-closed `throw` on unknown kind/staleness (`commandCodec.ts:104-106,125-128`). This is where #802 adds new event handling and where a snapshot/read decode would slot.

**Event flow**: worker → `EngineHost.nextEvent()` (`worker/engineHost.ts:48-51`, calls `readEvent`) → `serve.ts:50` pumps → posts `{type:'event',event}` → transport `emit()`. On the UI side, `LocalTransport` (`transport.ts:48-109`) correlates responses by monotonic id and calls `this.emit(message.event)` on `'event'` (`transport.ts:68`). `EngineFacade.subscribe(listener)` (`facade.ts:48-50`) exposes the stream.

**Read-path stubs**: **None exist.** `EngineFacade` (`facade.ts:16-127`) has one method per write command plus `start`/`logout`/`subscribe`/`manualRefresh` — no `snapshot()` / `read()` / `download()` method. `EngineTransport` interface (`transport.ts:23-32`) has only `start`/`command`/`subscribe`/`close`. `WasmEngineHandle` (`worker/engineWasm.ts:29-33`) exposes only `start`/`command`/`nextEvent`. #802 adds new methods across all four (`engineWasm.ts` handle type, `engineHost.ts`, `transport.ts`, `facade.ts`).

**Broadcast transport** `packages/client/src/broadcastTransport.ts`: follower-side `EngineTransport`. `command()` posts `cb:command` over `BroadcastChannel` (`broadcastTransport.ts:59-68`); receives `cb:response`/`cb:event` gated by a leader `token` (`broadcastTransport.ts:100-127`, `fromActiveLeader`). Leader side is `leaderRelay.ts` (fans engine events out as key-free `EventDescriptor`s, `leaderRelay.ts:11-13`). `LeaderMessage` union (`broadcast.ts:57-73`) carries `cb:response` and `cb:event{event:EventDescriptor}`. #802's snapshot/read read-paths must be added to both the request/response wire here and the leader relay — a follower cannot call the engine directly, so snapshot/read must round-trip through the leader.

**Test setup**:
- **Node/vitest unit tests** (`pnpm test` → `vitest run`): `facade.test.ts` (FakeTransport, `facade.test.ts:7-33`), `transport.test.ts` (FakeWorker replaying WorkerMessages, `transport.test.ts:6-36`), `broadcastTransport.test.ts`, `leadership.test.ts`, `engineClient.test.ts`, `index.test.ts`.
- **Browser conformance suite** (`pnpm test:browser` → `build-wasm.mjs` then `playwright test`; CI-blocking): in `packages/client/test/browser/`:
  - `conformance.spec.ts` — per-**seam** engine conformance kits over real IndexedDB/OPFS (floorStore, snapshotCache, stagingStore, credentialStore, scheduler, recordTransport) via a `window.runSeam` harness.
  - `engine.spec.ts` — the engine-worker RPC slice: cold-start/logout, out-of-order correlation, event-stream ordering, the `u64`/bigint + transfer boundary, WASM-backed detachment cases (via `window.runRealEngine`/`runBoundary`).
  - `leadership.spec.ts` — leader/follower.
  - The wasm build is driven by `test/browser/build-wasm.mjs` with `--features conformance` (`crates/wasm/src/conformance.rs`, gated at `lib.rs:47-48`). #802's snapshot/read boundary and the "direct + broadcast transport" conformance the issue references would extend `engine.spec.ts`/`leadership.spec.ts` here.

## 5. Blueprint normative guidance

**blueprint/engine.md:**
- Sync core state law — `engine.md:189-191`: *"rendered state = last-known-good remote snapshot ⊕ pending-op overlay, single owner; the op queue is the only local divergence (#33 D6)."*
- Focus-window tick — `engine.md:192-197`: *"refresh the vault pointer, the open folder, and its full ancestor chain to root"* — the exact focus/ancestor surface #802 projects.
- Ops list — `engine.md:208-209`: *"every mutation is an intent op — create, delete, rename, relink, updateContent — carrying its base sequence, journaled FIFO in the durable op queue."*
- Content plane reads — `engine.md:479-482`: *"the token-authed trustless gateway is a member accelerator; any public trustless gateway is the no-auth fallback. The engine verifies CIDs client-side via core on every block/CAR response; media uses ranged fetches."* (This is exactly what `read_content`/`download` will drive.)
- Facade — `engine.md:494-502`: *"one async command-and-event surface, designed to be wrapped, not extended: commands ... and an event stream out (snapshot updates, staleness transitions, withheld-update escalations, dead-letters, attributable abuse events). ... hosts render, they never decide."* No `SnapshotView`/`OpProgress` is named in the blueprint by that term — #802 introduces the vocabulary.

**blueprint/web-client.md:**
- UI state law — `web-client.md:138-144`: *"the facade emits snapshot updates with the pending-op overlay already applied **plus per-node pending/dead-letter flags**. The UI holds one mechanically derived subscription store ... with no independent writers."* — the normative basis for #802's per-node `pending`/`deadLetter`.
- Progressive hydration — `web-client.md:145-147`: *"name and kind render instantly from the parent's child refs (#27 D7); **size/mtime arrive as child resolves land in the snapshot** — no blocking resolution pass, no kind-flip UX."* — the normative basis for `size?`/`mtime?` being optional in `SnapshotView`.
- Routes key on node id — `web-client.md:148-150`: *"Routes key on the stable node id — never ipnsName ... the root is just the vault pointer's current root node."* — matches `SnapshotView`'s root id + ancestor chain.
- Download path — `web-client.md:195-197`: *"the engine fetches blocks (token-authed trustless gateway, public-gateway fallback), CID-verifies, unseals, and **returns a Blob**; the UI object-URLs it. Same path for previews."* — normative for `read_content -> Bytes`.
- Upload/op progress — `web-client.md:193-194`: *"Per-file progress/error is **event-stream state on the upload's op id**; cancel is a facade command killing the op before publish."* — the normative basis for #802's `OpProgress{opId,node,phase,error?}`.
- Wire hygiene — `web-client.md:96-98`: *"projections and events are plain structured-clone data; commands carry at most Blob/File handles."* And `web-client.md:114-117`: *"wasm-bindgen types end to end. Commands are the engine facade's commands verbatim; the client adds transport, never semantics."*
- Testing hooks — `web-client.md:229-239`: `packages/client` (leadership, failover, both transports, seams) is a **CI-blocking browser test surface**; a DEV-gated facade introspection hook (snapshot + event-stream taps, no key access) is the e2e seam.

## 6. Existing types named SnapshotView / OpProgress / read_content / download

- `OpProgress`: **none** (new in #802). Closest existing concept: `StageOutcome` (`sync/staging.rs`), `Event::DeadLetter`, `Event::RenewalFailed`.

I've verified the scout report against the code and traced every path the issue touches. Here is the implementation plan.

# Scout-report verification

Confirmed accurate (with evidence):
- `Engine<T: SeamTypes>` facade shape, `snapshot: Rc<RefCell<Snapshot>>`, unbounded events, metadata-only commands, `view()` FUSE-shaped — `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:593-1173`. Content-bearing create rejects Unimplemented at facade.rs:1046.
- `NodeMeta` has no size/mtime/content-CID — `crates/engine/src/sync/model.rs:22-36`. `project_root` discards `created_at`/`modified_at` — `crates/engine/src/sync/project.rs:26` — **and also discards `ChildRef.ipns_name`**, which matters more than the scout noted (it is the only way to locate a child's own record).
- Dead-letter: only cold-start decode failures, emitted then removed from the queue — facade.rs:852-864. No retained set, no node attribution.
- `read_block` fail-closed CID verify + plane pinning — `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:175-220`; `RootManifest{chunk_size,size,leaf_cids}` — `content/dag.rs`; `ContentKey` — `content/chunk.rs:24`.
- wasm `host.rs` exposes only `start`/`command`/`nextEvent` (host.rs:180-221); boundary pattern is opaque wasm-bindgen objects with `kind()` + per-variant getters (lib.rs:330-408). No serde-wasm-bindgen anywhere.
- `protocol.ts` `WorkerRequest` = start|command only; `CorrelatedTransport.Pending.resolve: () => void` (void-only responses, correlatedTransport.ts:17); broadcast wire has no read path.
- **`renewalFailed` missing from `EventDescriptor` is confirmed and is a live bug**: `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs:346` emits kind `"renewalFailed"`, `commandCodec.ts:110-129` throws on unknown kinds, and `serve.ts:54-56` converts the event-pump throw into `fatal`, terminally killing the transport. The first real `Event::RenewalFailed` bricks every tab. Must fix in this slice.

Inaccuracies / corrections:
1. **`open_chunk` is not in `content/chunk.rs`** — it lives in core: `crates/core/src/content/seal.rs:45`. The engine's chunk.rs only calls it in tests.
2. Understated: **`Staleness` is entirely dormant** — `sync/staleness.rs::classify` is a pure function with zero production callers; `Event::StalenessChanged` is never emitted anywhere; the engine tracks no `last_success`/`reconcile_in_flight`/connectivity state. `snapshot()`'s Staleness field needs new tracking state, not just a call into the classifier.
3. Scout said "No node→contentCid map exists" — true, but the deeper fact: **it structurally cannot exist from the root projection**. `ChildRef` is `{id, name, ipnsName, kind, linkCounter}` with explicitly "No key wraps, no size/mtime mirrors" (`crates/core/src/seal/body.rs:10-14`). Content refs live only in the file's **own** record (`ReadBody::File.versions[].{content_cid, content_key, size, modified_at}`, body.rs:140-150, 246-251).

# Decided answers to the 7 design questions

**Q1 — where `read_content` gets CID + key: resolve the file's own record on demand.** Evidence: `Version` (body.rs:140-150) carries `content_cid`, secret `content_key` (zeroizing, read via `Version::content_key()`, body.rs:172), `size`, `modified_at`; head of newest-first `versions` is current. Child records are *not* resolved anywhere today — only the root, via `RootAdopter` (net/adopter.rs:144) and the resolve tick (facade.rs:945-1019). Extending the Snapshot with content refs is impossible without resolving children anyway, so `read_content` resolves the child record on demand through a new reduced **`ChildAdopter`** (a non-scope-root record has no grant section — `Envelope` is `{v, id, epochTag, readSealed, writeSealed?, grantSection?}`, `crates/core/src/seal/envelope.rs:5` — so the full six-stage `gate::adopt` cannot apply; the child pipeline is: record verify → head-block fetch fail-closed on CID → envelope decode → `env.id == node` and `env.scope == scope` transplant checks → per-name sequence floor + scope read-epoch floor (`gate/floor.rs`) → AAD-bound `open_read_body` under `kdf::read_key(kdf::node_seed(scope_seed, node_id))`, mirroring RootAdopter's derivation at adopter.rs:171-172). The scope read seed is recovered by the owner arm at every root adopt (owner blob, adopter.rs:161-167) but currently dropped; retain it in a new engine-held `scope_read_seeds` map (in-engine key material only — nothing crosses the boundary; `read_content` returns plaintext `Vec<u8>`, key stays inside). Reuse `resolve()`/`resolve_gated` (net/resolve.rs:119) by implementing `Adopter` for `ChildAdopter`, which gives cache-first reads and snapshot-cache write-back for free. Two smaller decisions inside this: (a) `ChildRef.ipns_name` bytes are treated as the UTF-8 bytes of the canonical base36 name string, parsed fail-closed via `IpnsName::parse` — consistent with the existing convention that the snapshot cache keys on `name.as_str().as_bytes()` (resolve.rs:155) and `HeldRecord.routing_key: String`; (b) a child envelope that *does* carry a grant section (a nested scope root) fails closed in v1 — granted-subscope reads land with the grants slice.

**Q2 — size/mtime: project what exists, leave children `None`.** `ChildRef` carries neither (body.rs:14), so focused-folder children project `size: None, mtime: None` — matching blueprint/web-client.md:145-147 progressive hydration ("name and kind render instantly from the parent's child refs; size/mtime arrive as child resolves land"). Two things hydrate now: the folder's own `modified_at` (currently discarded at project.rs:26) is projected onto the folder node; and after a successful `read_content` adopt, the file's head-version `size`/`modified_at` are folded into the base snapshot (a gate-passing adopt, so it may legally touch the snapshot) with a `SnapshotUpdated` emit. Bulk child-resolve hydration (focus-window tick over children) is a follow-up.

**Q3 — per-node pending/deadLetter: pending from the queue, dead-letter from a new retained set, honestly limited.** `pending` = node ids appearing as `Op.target` in the decoded durable queue (`Op.target: NodeId`, sync/op.rs:25) — computed at `snapshot()` time from the same `pending_ops()` read that feeds the overlay, so flag and overlay are consistent. Dead letters: the engine currently deletes the queue row and forgets (facade.rs:852-864); add `dead_letters: Rc<RefCell<BTreeMap<OpId, Option<NodeId>>>>` retained for the session, populated at the cold-start dead-letter site (node = `None` — an undecodable op cannot name its target) and by future rebase dead-letters (which will know the node). `SnapshotView` gets per-child `dead_letter: bool` (true iff some retained entry maps `Some(node)`) plus a top-level `dead_letters: Vec<OpId>` list so hosts can render the persistent notice today. The per-node flag is structurally wired but stays false until the rebase slice attributes nodes — stated in docs, not papered over.

**Q4 — OpProgress: a new `Event` variant on the existing stream, download phases live, upload phases dormant.** blueprint/web-client.md:193 ("per-file progress/error is event-stream state on the upload's op id") pins it to the one event stream — no second channel, no new worker pump. Shape: `Event::OpProgress { op_id: Option<OpId>, node: NodeId, phase: OpPhase, error: Option<String> }` with `OpPhase { DownloadStarted, DownloadCompleted, DownloadFailed }` now (`op_id` is `Option` because downloads don't ride the op queue; upload phases — Staged/Sealing/Uploading/Published, with a real `op_id` — are added by the content-plane slice). Emission points: entry/exit/error of `read_content`.

**Q5 — `snapshot(folder)` is a parameterized pure read, independent of SetFocus.** Signature `Engine::snapshot(&self, folder: NodeId) -> Result<SnapshotView, EngineError>` over the rendered view (base ⊕ overlay, same `render()` as `view()`, facade.rs:1108). `SetFocus` remains a separate (still-Unimplemented) command; the issue's "key-free projection from sync/model::Snapshot" confirms no network, no focus coupling. Fail-closed: folder absent from the rendered view → new `EngineError::UnknownNode`; present but `kind == File` → new `EngineError::NotAFolder`. Note honestly: for a non-root folder, base children aren't resolved yet (only the root's direct children project today), so a subfolder shows overlay-created children only until the child-resolve/focus-window slice — correct behavior, documented.

**Q6 — broadcast read path: `cb:read` request / `cb:response` with payload; download bytes as `Blob`.** Followers round-trip reads through the leader: new `FollowerMessage` `{ type: 'cb:read'; clientId; requestId; read: {kind:'snapshot'; folder: Uint8Array} | {kind:'download'; node: Uint8Array} }`; the ok-`cb:response` gains `result?: SnapshotDescriptor` and `content?: Blob`. Snapshot views are small plain data (structured clone fine). Download bytes ride a `Blob`, not a raw `ArrayBuffer`/`Uint8Array`: BroadcastChannel structured-clones per receiving context, and `Blob`'s immutable backing store is shared — exactly the rationale already used for uploads in `hoistContent` (broadcast.ts:90-101, "no byte copies"). The follower converts via `blob.arrayBuffer()`. Note the plaintext-over-broadcast question for the crypto-privacy review: same-origin is the stated trust boundary, and leader→follower events already ride this channel; download plaintext is the *user's own* content going to the user's own same-origin tab — but the review should confirm, and the leader must only answer `cb:read` (it already token-stamps responses so followers reject forgeries).

**Q7 — WASM boundary: opaque wasm-bindgen objects with getters, converted to plain descriptors in the worker codec.** The repo's pattern is explicit and two-layered: `crates/wasm` exposes opaque handle types with key-free getters (`Event` with `kind()` + per-variant getters, lib.rs:330-408; u64→`bigint`, `Vec<u8>`→`Uint8Array`), and `packages/client`'s worker codec reads them into plain structured-clone descriptors for the wire (protocol.ts header: "Everything here is plain structured-clone data" — satisfying web-client.md:96-98). I've verified the scout report against the code and traced every path the issue touches. Here is the implementation plan.

# Scout-report verification

Confirmed accurate (with evidence):
- `Engine<T: SeamTypes>` facade shape, `snapshot: Rc<RefCell<Snapshot>>`, unbounded events, metadata-only commands, `view()` FUSE-shaped — `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:593-1173`. Content-bearing create rejects Unimplemented at facade.rs:1046.
- `NodeMeta` has no size/mtime/content-CID — `crates/engine/src/sync/model.rs:22-36`. `project_root` discards `created_at`/`modified_at` — `crates/engine/src/sync/project.rs:26` — **and also discards `ChildRef.ipns_name`**, which matters more than the scout noted (it is the only way to locate a child's own record).
- Dead-letter: only cold-start decode failures, emitted then removed from the queue — facade.rs:852-864. No retained set, no node attribution.
- `read_block` fail-closed CID verify + plane pinning — `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:175-220`; `RootManifest{chunk_size,size,leaf_cids}` — `content/dag.rs`; `ContentKey` — `content/chunk.rs:24`.
- wasm `host.rs` exposes only `start`/`command`/`nextEvent` (host.rs:180-221); boundary pattern is opaque wasm-bindgen objects with `kind()` + per-variant getters (lib.rs:330-408). No serde-wasm-bindgen anywhere.
- `protocol.ts` `WorkerRequest` = start|command only; `CorrelatedTransport.Pending.resolve: () => void` (void-only responses, correlatedTransport.ts:17); broadcast wire has no read path.
- **`renewalFailed` missing from `EventDescriptor` is confirmed and is a live bug**: `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs:346` emits kind `"renewalFailed"`, `commandCodec.ts:110-129` throws on unknown kinds, and `serve.ts:54-56` converts the event-pump throw into `fatal`, terminally killing the transport. The first real `Event::RenewalFailed` bricks every tab. Must fix in this slice.

Inaccuracies / corrections:
1. **`open_chunk` is not in `content/chunk.rs`** — it lives in core: `crates/core/src/content/seal.rs:45`. The engine's chunk.rs only calls it in tests.
2. Understated: **`Staleness` is entirely dormant** — `sync/staleness.rs::classify` is a pure function with zero production callers; `Event::StalenessChanged` is never emitted anywhere; the engine tracks no `last_success`/`reconcile_in_flight`/connectivity state. `snapshot()`'s Staleness field needs new tracking state, not just a call into the classifier.
3. Scout said "No node→contentCid map exists" — true, but the deeper fact: **it structurally cannot exist from the root projection**. `ChildRef` is `{id, name, ipnsName, kind, linkCounter}` with explicitly "No key wraps, no size/mtime mirrors" (`crates/core/src/seal/body.rs:10-14`). Content refs live only in the file's **own** record (`ReadBody::File.versions[].{content_cid, content_key, size, modified_at}`, body.rs:140-150, 246-251).

# Decided answers to the 7 design questions

**Q1 — where `read_content` gets CID + key: resolve the file's own record on demand.** Evidence: `Version` (body.rs:140-150) carries `content_cid`, secret `content_key` (zeroizing, read via `Version::content_key()`, body.rs:172), `size`, `modified_at`; head of newest-first `versions` is current. Child records are *not* resolved anywhere today — only the root, via `RootAdopter` (net/adopter.rs:144) and the resolve tick (facade.rs:945-1019). Extending the Snapshot with content refs is impossible without resolving children anyway, so `read_content` resolves the child record on demand through a new reduced **`ChildAdopter`** (a non-scope-root record has no grant section — `Envelope` is `{v, id, epochTag, readSealed, writeSealed?, grantSection?}`, `crates/core/src/seal/envelope.rs:5` — so the full six-stage `gate::adopt` cannot apply; the child pipeline is: record verify → head-block fetch fail-closed on CID → envelope decode → `env.id == node` and `env.scope == scope` transplant checks → per-name sequence floor + scope read-epoch floor (`gate/floor.rs`) → AAD-bound `open_read_body` under `kdf::read_key(kdf::node_seed(scope_seed, node_id))`, mirroring RootAdopter's derivation at adopter.rs:171-172). The scope read seed is recovered by the owner arm at every root adopt (owner blob, adopter.rs:161-167) but currently dropped; retain it in a new engine-held `scope_read_seeds` map (in-engine key material only — nothing crosses the boundary; `read_content` returns plaintext `Vec<u8>`, key stays inside). Reuse `resolve()`/`resolve_gated` (net/resolve.rs:119) by implementing `Adopter` for `ChildAdopter`, which gives cache-first reads and snapshot-cache write-back for free. Two smaller decisions inside this: (a) `ChildRef.ipns_name` bytes are treated as the UTF-8 bytes of the canonical base36 name string, parsed fail-closed via `IpnsName::parse` — consistent with the existing convention that the snapshot cache keys on `name.as_str().as_bytes()` (resolve.rs:155) and `HeldRecord.routing_key: String`; (b) a child envelope that *does* carry a grant section (a nested scope root) fails closed in v1 — granted-subscope reads land with the grants slice.

**Q2 — size/mtime: project what exists, leave children `None`.** `ChildRef` carries neither (body.rs:14), so focused-folder children project `size: None, mtime: None` — matching blueprint/web-client.md:145-147 progressive hydration ("name and kind render instantly from the parent's child refs; size/mtime arrive as child resolves land"). Two things hydrate now: the folder's own `modified_at` (currently discarded at project.rs:26) is projected onto the folder node; and after a successful `read_content` adopt, the file's head-version `size`/`modified_at` are folded into the base snapshot (a gate-passing adopt, so it may legally touch the snapshot) with a `SnapshotUpdated` emit. Bulk child-resolve hydration (focus-window tick over children) is a follow-up.

**Q3 — per-node pending/deadLetter: pending from the queue, dead-letter from a new retained set, honestly limited.** `pending` = node ids appearing as `Op.target` in the decoded durable queue (`Op.target: NodeId`, sync/op.rs:25) — computed at `snapshot()` time from the same `pending_ops()` read that feeds the overlay, so flag and overlay are consistent. ## Summary

Closes the facade read-surface gap that blocks the web browser UI: the engine was command-in / event-out only, with a payload-free `SnapshotUpdated`. This lands the key-free read surface end to end — engine projection, WASM boundary, and both client transports.

### Engine (`crates/engine`)

- `Engine::snapshot(folder) -> SnapshotView` — key-free projection over the rendered view (base ⊕ pending-op overlay): root id, focused-folder direct children `{id, name, kind, size?, mtime?, pending, deadLetter, contentVersion}`, breadcrumb ancestor chain, retained dead letters, and the current `Staleness` rung. Fail-closed on unknown nodes and non-folders.
- `Engine::read_content(node) -> Bytes` — resolves the file's own record via a new `ChildAdopter` (record verify → CID-verified head fetch → envelope decode → transplant checks → sequence/read-epoch floors → AAD-bound unseal under the node-derived read key; grant-bearing child envelopes fail closed), then fetches the content DAG through the gateway set with per-block CID verification, cross-checks manifest vs version size, opens each chunk, and returns plaintext. The owner scope read seed recovered at root adopts is now retained in memory (never persisted, never crosses the facade).
- Staleness tracking is now live: the resolve tick stamps successes via the scheduler seam, classifies the rung, and emits `StalenessChanged` on transitions (previously the classifier had no callers and the event no emitter).
- Dead letters are retained for the session and surfaced in `SnapshotView`; per-child attribution stays false until the rebase slice can name targets.
- `Event::OpProgress { opId?, node, phase, error? }` with download phases; upload phases join the content-plane slice.
- Successful downloads fold head-version `size`/`mtime` into the base snapshot and emit `SnapshotUpdated` (progressive hydration).

### WASM boundary (`crates/wasm`)

`EngineHandle.snapshot` / `EngineHandle.download`, plus `SnapshotView` / `SnapshotChild` / `Breadcrumb` / `OpPhase` boundary types with key-free getters following the existing conventions (u64 → bigint, ids → Uint8Array, Option → undefined).

### Client (`packages/client`)

- Worker protocol/codec/serve gain `snapshot` and `download` requests; download bytes transfer worker → UI and ride a shared-backing `Blob` leader → follower over the broadcast channel.
- `EngineTransport`, `LocalTransport`, `BroadcastTransport`, leader relay, `EngineClient`, and `EngineFacade` all gain the read paths; followers round-trip reads through the leader under the existing token gating.
- **Bug fix:** `renewalFailed` was emitted by the engine but missing from `EventDescriptor` — the fail-closed codec throw turned the event pump fatal, bricking every tab's transport on the first real renewal failure. It is now mirrored and reaches subscribers.

## Tests

- Engine: snapshot projection, staleness transitions under the virtual scheduler, dead-letter retention, and a full `read_content` capstone (happy path, tampered leaf, transplant, grant-bearing child, replay of an older sequence, size mismatches, availability vs trust classification) — all seam-driven, no clocks/RNG.
- WASM: native exhaustive-match guards plus wasm32 boundary tests (bigint/Uint8Array/undefined shapes).
- Client: 62 vitest cases including read/command correlation, renewalFailed pump survival, broadcast round-trips with forged-token rejection and Blob byte-equality; 19 Playwright browser tests including the new read-path conformance over both transports against the real WASM engine.

## Deferred (with rationale)

- `Staleness::Offline` rung — no connectivity seam exists yet; classifier input stays `Online`.
- Node-attributed dead letters — undecodable ops cannot name a target; attribution lands with the live-rebase slice.
- Upload `OpProgress` phases — content-bearing commands are still unimplemented.
- Focused-subfolder child hydration via the focus-window tick — `ChildAdopter` is the reusable piece.
- Granted-subscope child reads — fail closed now, grants slice later.

Closes #802
Part of #642

Efficiency review of `git diff main...HEAD` (feat/engine-snapshot-and-read-surface). Findings, most impactful first:

1. **`/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/crates/wasm/src/host.rs:233-241` (and 216-224)** — The engine mutex is held across the entire download/snapshot await: `engine.lock().await.read_content(node).await` keeps the `futures_util::lock::Mutex` guard alive for the whole multi-leaf network fetch.
   - Cost: one large file download serializes every other engine call — snapshot paints, commands, other downloads — behind potentially seconds of network I/O; the module doc even advertises reads "share the mutex, so concurrent calls queue".
   - Cheaper: the read paths take `&self` on `Engine`; use an async `RwLock` (read for `snapshot`/`read_content`, write for `start`/`command`), or narrow the guard to the synchronous setup and drop it before the leaf-fetch loop.

2. **`/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1426`** — `read_content_inner` calls `self.render().await?` — a full durable staging-store read, whole-queue `decode_queue`, and `apply_overlay` (which starts with `base.clone()`, cloning the entire snapshot tree) — only to look up one node's `kind` + `ipns_name`.
   - Cost: O(tree + queue) allocation and decode per file read, on the hot download path.
   - Cheaper: check `self.snapshot.borrow().node(node)` first (published nodes always live in the base); fall back to the pending-ops read only when the node is absent, purely to distinguish `ContentUnavailable` (pending create) from `UnknownNode`.

Review complete. Findings below — simplification angle only, ordered most valuable first.

1. **`crates/engine/src/sync/boot.rs:63`** — `ColdStartSinks` bundles two `&mut dyn FnMut` callbacks where a return value does the same job.
   Cost: a new public struct, awkward `(sinks.emit)(...)` call syntax, a closure pair + struct assembly at both call sites (facade.rs:1052-1062, boot.rs test:427), and an extra `Rc` clone in the facade. The `deposit_read_seed` sink narrows nothing — the callback receives the exact same seed the caller would.
   Simpler: add `read_scope_seed: Option<Zeroizing<[u8; 32]>>` to `ColdStartOutcome` (it is consumed immediately in `Engine::start`, which owns the seed map and deposits right there) and keep `emit` as the plain `&mut dyn FnMut(Event)` parameter it was. Deletes the struct and all closure plumbing; the seed is in-memory and zeroizing either way.

2. **`crates/engine/src/net/resolve.rs:147`** — `resolve_with_read_seed` is a pub(crate) wrapper whose entire body destructures `resolve_gated`.
   Cost: a fourth entry point over the same core (`resolve`, `resolve_with_read_seed`, `resolve_and_hold`), plus a doc block and an extra `net/mod.rs` re-export, for one caller (boot.rs:201).
   Simpler: make `resolve_gated`/`GatedResolve` pub(crate) and destructure at the caller — or fold this into finding 1, where cold-start no longer needs a seed-bearing resolve variant at all if the seed rides `AdoptOutcome` → outcome as it already does for `resolve_and_hold`.

3. **`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:423`** — comment on `Event::OpProgress` ("Emitters land with the content pipeline slice; the variant is the contract") is an absence-justifying comment that is also false in this same diff.
   Cost: `read_content` emits this variant at facade.rs:1571, so the comment misleads reviewers today and rots further with each emitter. This is the exact shape the repo rule bans.
   Simpler: delete the sentence; describe what the variant carries.

4. **`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:427`** — `OpProgress.op_id: Option<OpId>` is speculative: no emitter ever produces `Some` (the one emitter, `emit_op_progress` at facade.rs:1570, hardcodes `None`).
   Cost: dead plumbing across three layers — the wasm `op_id` getter's `OpProgress` arm (crates/wasm/src/lib.rs), the TS protocol `opId: bigint | null`, the codec mapping, and tests exercising both the `Some` and `None` cases of a value that cannot occur.
   Simpler: drop the field until an op-driven emitter lands (adding an optional field later is a compatible change at every one of these boundaries).

5. **`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1480-1493`** — the `Current` and `NoUpdate`/`Some` arms are copy-paste: both call `adopter.open_at_floor(&name, bytes).await.map_err(EngineError::from_gate)`.
   Cost: duplicated fallible pipeline; a future change to the at-floor path must be made twice.
   Simpler: select the bytes first (`Current { record_bytes } => record_bytes`, `NoUpdate => resolved.last_known_good.ok_or(...)?`), then one `open_at_floor` call. Also facade.rs:1495-1499: the `TrustViolation(rejection)` arm re-implements `EngineError::from_gate`'s `Rejected` arm — `EngineError::from_gate(GateError::Rejected(rejection))` reuses it.

6. **`packages/client/src/broadcast.ts:81-82`** — the ok-`cb:response` carries two optional payload fields (`result?: SnapshotDescriptor`, `content?: Blob`) that are mutually exclusive by construction.
   Cost: the reader must coalesce (`response.content ?? response.result`, broadcastTransport.ts:136), and the type admits an impossible both-set state.
   Simpler: one field, `result?: SnapshotDescriptor | Blob`; the leader relay puts the Blob there and the reader passes `response.result` straight to `settle`.

7. **`packages/client/test/browser/engine.spec.ts:19`** — the diff adds three copy-pasted test declarations: `SnapshotSuiteResult` (duplicated at engineHarness.ts:25), `SnapshotResult` (leadership.spec.ts:13 / leadership.ts:23), and a byte-identical `hex()` helper (engineHarness.ts:106 / leadership.ts:67).
   Cost: four interfaces + two helpers to keep manually in sync; a field added to the harness result silently no-ops in the spec's copy.
   Simpler: `import type` the result interfaces from the harness modules into the specs (type-only imports are erased, so the browser/node split is unaffected), and put `hex`/`unhex` in one shared browser-test util.

8. **`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1354`** — `dead.values().any(|node| *node == Some(child.id))` runs a linear scan of the dead-letter map per child.
   Cost: O(children × dead letters) per snapshot read, and the intent ("is this node dead-lettered") is buried in an `Option` comparison.
   Simpler: build `let dead_nodes: BTreeSet<NodeId> = dead.values().flatten().copied().collect();` once beside the `pending` set (same shape, symmetric code) and use `dead_nodes.contains(&child.id)`.

Otherwise the diff is clean for this angle: the `GatedResolve` named struct replacing the 3-tuple, the `ChildAdopter` assembled-envelope cache (saves a real head-block re-fetch on the steady-state path), the `pub(super)` widening of the `net::adopter` reject helpers, and the `request<T>`/`dispatch` split in `correlatedTransport.ts` (three existing void call sites) are all justified as written.

- File: `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/crates/wasm/src/host.rs`, line 261 (`engine_error` → `JsError::new(&error.to_string())`); also `packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts:129` (`error: string`), `leaderRelay.ts:142`.

- File: `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/crates/engine/src/net/child.rs`, line 113-117

- File: `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/crates/engine/src/net/resolve.rs`, lines 147 (`resolve_with_read_seed`), 282 (`resolve_and_hold` now returning a tuple), plus `AdoptOutcome.read_scope_seed`

**6. Child-ref `ipnsName` wire validation deferred to the innermost consumer**
- File: `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/crates/engine/src/facade.rs`, line 1439
- Summary: `project.rs` stores the `ChildRef` ipnsName as opaque `Option<Vec<u8>>` in `NodeMeta`; the facade re-parses UTF-8 → `IpnsName` on every read and classifies failure as `TrustViolation`.
- Cost: A malformed ref passes the adoption gate and only rejects when the user opens the file; every future consumer of `NodeMeta.ipns_name` (focus-window child polling, desktop FUSE) must re-parse and remember the trust classification.
- Deeper form: validate once where gate-passing state is projected (`project_root`, or core's `ChildRef` decode) and store a typed `Option<IpnsName>` — fail closed at the boundary, parse never again.

**7. Read path writes base-snapshot projection state inline**
- File: `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/crates/engine/src/facade.rs`, lines 1403-1409
- Summary: `read_content` folds the verified head version's size/mtime into the base via direct `snapshot.borrow_mut().node_mut(node)` in the facade, while all other adopted-body → base projection lives in `sync/project.rs` (`project_root`).
- Cost: Two writers of projection state in two idioms; the "only gate-passing state touches the base" law is now enforced by convention in the facade rather than by the projection module; a child-folder read (next slice) will need a third copy.
- Deeper form: `project::project_child_version(snapshot, node, size, mtime)` beside `project_root`, so `sync/project.rs` stays the single home for base-snapshot mutation from adopted bodies.

**8. Per-read-kind optional payload fields on the generic response ack**
- File: `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/packages/client/src/broadcast.ts`, line 81 (`result?: SnapshotDescriptor; content?: Blob`); same shape at `worker/protocol.ts:128` (`result?: SnapshotDescriptor | ArrayBuffer`); disambiguated by `response.content ?? response.result` at `broadcastTransport.ts:136`
- Summary: The generic ok-ack grew two parallel read-specific optional fields instead of one opaque payload slot; nothing binds the response payload shape to the request kind (`request<T>`'s cast is unchecked).
- Cost: A third read kind grows a third optional field and another `??` clause; a response carrying the wrong field resolves the wrong-typed promise silently.
- Deeper form: since the correlation layer is already type-erased (`Pending.resolve(result: unknown)`), give the ack a single `result?: unknown` slot (Blob wrapping stays a leader-side transport detail), or echo the `WireRead` kind in the response and assert it at settle — one mechanism instead of accreting per-kind fields that pretend to a type safety the pending map cannot deliver.

## Clean areas
- `correlatedTransport.ts` `request<T>`/`dispatch` — the mechanism was generalized rather than special-cased; correct.
- `ChildAdopter`'s `assembled` memo mirrors the existing `RootAdopter` pattern — consistent, not a new special case.
- The wasm layer (`crates/wasm/src/lib.rs`, `host.rs`) contains zero projection/semantics — pure getter mirroring, right depth.
- `snapshot()`'s inline `pending_ops + apply_overlay` (rather than reusing `render()`) is justified: the single ops read feeds both overlay and pending flags, and the code says so once.
- `GatedResolve` replacing the 3-tuple is itself a good altitude fix within the constraint of finding 5.

**Child pipeline (`crates/engine/src/net/child.rs`) vs root gate — no bypass found.**
- Ordering is correct: record verify (Ed25519 key from the name) → CID-verified head fetch → grant-section reject → id/scope transplant check → floor checks → unseal → floor advance *only after* AAD-confirmed unseal (`ChildAdopter::adopt`, child.rs:170-199). The floor law is respected; `open_at_floor` never advances floors.
- The binding chain is closed end-to-end: the child's `ipnsName` and `id` both come from the parent's sealed (AAD-bound) `ChildRef`; the record must verify against that name; the envelope's `id`/`scope` are explicitly checked against the expected node/scope (child.rs:130-136) *and* independently AAD-bound in `open_read_body` (envelope.rs:122-146 binds `(v, id, scope, epoch, struct-tag)`), so a forged epoch, transplanted id, or foreign scope cannot unseal. A folder body under a file `ChildRef` is rejected post-unseal (facade.rs `read_content_inner`, kind transplant check).
- `has_grant_section` is deliberately stricter than `grant_section_bytes` (key presence, any value type), so a non-bytes `grantSection` cannot smuggle a scope root through the child path.
- The floor refactor (`floor::check`, floor.rs:167-232) is behavior-preserving for the root gate (`epoch` at adoption.rs:461 is `candidate.envelope.epoch`); `Strictness::AtFloor` still rejects `sequence < floor` (replay) and always enforces the read-epoch (revocation) floor on the re-open path.
- Cached-record paths (`Current`, `NoUpdate` → `last_known_good`) re-run the *full* pipeline via `open_at_floor` — cached bytes are never trusted; the `assembled` reuse cache is keyed by exact `(name, record_bytes)` equality within a single per-call adopter.

**Content read (`content/mod.rs::open_content`).** The whole DAG is anchored in the sealed read-body's `Version` (content CID + per-version key): root block CID-verified, manifest size cross-checked against the sealed version size, each leaf CID-verified then AEAD-opened under the version key, reassembled length re-checked. A network attacker cannot reorder, splice, or substitute leaves without breaking a CID or the AEAD. Confirmed the tampered-leaf test covers the fail-closed arm.

**Key/seed handling.** `read_scope_seed` rides only crate-internal structs (`AdoptOutcome` has no `Debug` derive; `GatedResolve` is `pub(crate)`; `ColdStartOutcome` hand-writes `Debug` with `<redacted>`), lands in the in-memory `scope_read_seeds` BTreeMap of `Zeroizing` values, and never reaches `Resolved`, events, error strings, or the wasm boundary. A missing seed fails **closed** (`read_content_inner` errors rather than skipping the unseal). Error `Display` strings carry check names/sizes only.

**Wasm/web boundary.** `snapshot`/`download` cross only key-free view state and user-requested plaintext; the error `code` is a fixed match-arm string set via `Reflect::set`, no injection surface. On the BroadcastChannel, the leader-token gate on `cb:response`/`cb:event` is unchanged in strength; the new read path means download plaintext (as a `Blob`) is observable by every listener on the channel — but `BroadcastChannel` is same-origin-partitioned, and any same-origin script could equally issue its own `cb:read` or `cb:leader`, so this adds no privilege beyond what same-origin compromise already grants (out of threat model). Follower reads are served without per-tab authorization, which matches the existing command path.

**Non-security observations (not findings, for awareness):** (1) a lazy-rotation-wave child sealed at an epoch below the scope's advanced read-epoch floor will fail closed as a trust violation — an availability sharp edge, correctly on the strict side; (2) `serve.ts::errorCode` accepts a `code` string off any thrown value, so a non-engine error with a `code` property could be misclassified by the client — cosmetic; (3) the transplant rejection reuses `GateStage::Unseal`/`SealOpenFailed` rather than a dedicated stage — diagnostic granularity only.

Review produced code through the lens of a cryptography and security testing expert. This command evaluates cryptographic implementations, validates security assumptions, and generates comprehensive test cases and edge cases.

<execution_context>

## Project Security Rules

Reference the project's AGENTS.md security rules:

- Never store privateKey in localStorage/sessionStorage
- Never log sensitive keys
- Never send unencrypted keys to server
- Always use ECIES for key wrapping
- Always use AES-256-GCM for content encryption
- Server NEVER has access to plaintext or unencrypted keys
- Always encrypt ipnsPrivateKey with TEE public key before sending
- TEE decrypts IPNS keys in hardware only, signs, and immediately discards

## Cryptographic Standards

| Algorithm      | Use Case           | Notes                              |
| -------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| AES-256-GCM    | Content encryption | Authenticated encryption required  |
| ECIES          | Key wrapping       | For asymmetric key transport       |
